title: Example 289 fixed-security through the adapter entry: the frozen claim on Spring Security 5.6.4, expected established
description: The frozen claim claims/protected-prefix-matched-across-line-terminators.json, unchanged, run by examples/289-spring-security-cve-2022-22978-regex-request-matcher-bypass/proofs/prove.py: jvmcontract prove (own checker, strict gaps). The entry is example289.adapter.RegexMatchAdapter#matches(String pattern, boolean caseInsensitive, String servletPath, String pathInfo, String query), the one the claim's first assumption names: it builds the original RegexRequestMatcher(pattern, null, caseInsensitive) and asks matches of a request carrying the three Strings (example289.carrier.PathOnlyRequest). The claim's expressions are passed as they are written, compiled by javac and run as bytecode, at the claim's bound of 8 code units for each String; loops are followed exactly for 26 turns, the longest any can go (the URL is three Strings and a '?'). The class path is the revision's five pinned JARs, each checked against its SHA-256. This is a proof beside the example route, which takes no adapter entry (each task's invocation in target.json says so). Nothing is put in a method's place and no lemma is given: the constructor and matches run as the release's bytecode, so the flags are the ones the release computes. What changed in the verifier for it (lib/src/bmc/regex.rs): Pattern.compile(String, int) of a String that is an input is modelled where the solver shows that on the path it can only be characters that stand for themselves followed by '.*' (the Pattern is then those characters as a quoted text and '.' any number of times; any other pattern stays the JDK's call, a gap refused by name); the flags CASE_INSENSITIVE and DOTALL are formulas, so a constructor may choose them by an input; one '.*' that ends an expression takes surrogates, where matching by unit is the JDK's matching by code point. Beside it: Character.isLetter of an ASCII char, IntStream.range for the claim's own expression, and Logger.isLoggable below INFO as false under a stated assumption (the matcher's debug line through spring-jcl is not written). Each rule is proved to be its definition written out in Java on every input of a bound and the definition sampled against the JDK on a JVM (lib/tests/claims.rs, claims.P). The claim's predicates as javac compiles them agree with the oracle on all 44 probes (examples/289-spring-security-cve-2022-22978-regex-request-matcher-bypass/proofs/predicates.py). 5.6.4 compiles the pattern with DOTALL in both case modes; expected established: a literal prefix and '.*' matches every URL that begins with the prefix, whatever follows.

resources.notes: an inline probe at this bound took 28 s (1,003 paths); at bounds 4 and 6, 1 s and 7 s. The time besides is the release build of lib/ if its tree isn't cached and the fetch of the JARs
